_**Hit Me Hard and Soft**_ is the third studio album by American singer-songwriter [Billie Eilish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Eilish "Billie Eilish"), released on May 17, 2024, through Darkroom and [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"). She co-wrote it with her brother and frequent collaborator, [Finneas O'Connell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finneas_O'Connell "Finneas O'Connell"), who also serves as its producer. Stylistically, it has been labeled an [alternative pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_pop "Alternative pop") and [bedroom pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedroom_pop "Bedroom pop") record.
_Hit Me Hard and Soft_ received universal acclaim from critics who praised the production, songwriting, and vocal performances. It topped the charts in over 20 countries, including Australia, Canada, Germany, Ireland, New Zealand, Spain, and the United Kingdom. In the United States, it peaked at number two on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and charted all 10 of its songs in the top 40 of the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). It spawned four singles: "[Lunch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunch_\(song\) "Lunch \(song\)")", "[Birds of a Feather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birds_of_a_Feather_\(Billie_Eilish_song\) "Birds of a Feather \(Billie Eilish song\)")", "[Chihiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\) "Chihiro \(song\)")", and "[Wildflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildflower_\(Billie_Eilish_song\) "Wildflower \(Billie Eilish song\)")", all of which achieved commercial success. To support the album, Eilish embarked on [Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft:_The_Tour "Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour") from September 2024 to November 2025. [A concert film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Eilish_%E2%80%93_Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft:_The_Tour_\(Live_in_3D\) "Billie Eilish – Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour \(Live in 3D\)") documenting its [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester") shows was theatrically released in May 2026 and received a [Best Music Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Music_Film "Best Music Film") nomination at the [69th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/69th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "69th Annual Grammy Awards"). 
At the [67th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "67th Annual Grammy Awards"), the album and its songs received a total of seven nominations, including [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year"), [Best Pop Vocal Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Vocal_Album "Best Pop Vocal Album"), [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_the_Year "Song of the Year"), and [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_of_the_Year "Record of the Year"). "Wildflower" won Song of the Year at [the following ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/68th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "68th Annual Grammy Awards"), making Eilish and O'Connell the artists with the most wins in the category. They also tied [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele"), [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars"), and [Paul Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Simon "Paul Simon") for the most wins in the General Field, with seven each.
## Background and recording
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and recording")]
Eilish co-wrote and recorded her second studio album, _[Happier Than Ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happier_Than_Ever "Happier Than Ever")_ , at her brother [Finneas O'Connell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finneas_O'Connell "Finneas O'Connell")'s home recording studio, located in the basement of his [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") residence.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-2) Recording took place weekly between April 2020 and February 2021, with the track listing finalized by the duo during creation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-4) Released on July 30, 2021,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-5) _Happier Than Ever_ was met with critical acclaim and commercial success, topping the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-6) and receiving two nominations at the [64th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "64th Annual Grammy Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-7) Eilish surprise-released her second extended play, _[Guitar Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar_Songs "Guitar Songs")_ , in July 2022. The following year, she released "[What Was I Made For?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Was_I_Made_For%3F "What Was I Made For?")" for [the soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_the_Album "Barbie the Album") to the fantasy-comedy film _[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_\(film\) "Barbie \(film\)")_ (2023); she was inspired to write the song after seeing unfinished scenes of the film during its production.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-8) The song won the [Academy Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song") and [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") for [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_the_Year "Song of the Year") and [Best Song Written for Visual Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Song_Written_for_Visual_Media "Best Song Written for Visual Media").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-9)
Eilish began formulating ideas for her third studio album with O'Connell in December 2021.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-10) In an interview with [Zane Lowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zane_Lowe "Zane Lowe") for [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music"), she mentioned that she hoped to start writing it in 2023.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-11) In December 2023, Eilish said on _[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")_ that it was "almost done".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-12) Three months later, she confirmed that it had been [mastered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastering_\(audio\) "Mastering \(audio\)").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-Eilish-1)
### Artwork
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Artwork")]
The album art, which was shot by underwater photographer William Drumm, depicts Eilish falling through a door frame into dark blue water. Eilish described the photoshoot, which took six hours to complete and involved her being repeatedly submerged for two minutes at a time with a weight attached to her shoulders and without goggles or nose plugs,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-rsalbumart-13) as being one of the most painful experiences of her life.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-rsalbumart-13)

### Music and themes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Music and themes")]
Musically, _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ has been described as an [alternative pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_pop "Alternative pop")[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-Slant-15) and [bedroom pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedroom_pop "Bedroom pop")[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-16) record with influences of [electronic music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-ap-17) [soft rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_rock "Soft rock"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-hs-19) [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz"),[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-al-20)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-ap-17) [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music"),[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-tr-21)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-ap-17) and [orchestral music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchestral_music "Orchestral music").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-hs-19) Lyrically, it addresses themes of romantic disappointment, desire, [body image](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_image "Body image"), depression, fame, betrayal, anxiety, [mental illness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_illness "Mental illness"), romance, death, unhealthy relationship dynamics, isolation, emotional distance, heartbreak, and acceptance. French critic [Le Monde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Monde "Le Monde") framed it as a turn toward romantic tenderness while retaining the darker, more haunting qualities of Eilish's earlier work.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-tr-21)
Critics described the album as cohesive yet eclectic alt-pop that shifts from subdued [acoustic guitars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustic_guitar "Acoustic guitar"), softer electronic pulses, and [ambient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambient_music "Ambient music") soundscapes to harsher [bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_\(sound\) "Bass \(sound\)") drops, [dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_music "Dance music")-influenced passages, and rock [crescendos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crescendo "Crescendo").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-hs-19)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-Slant-15) [Amanda Petrusich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Petrusich "Amanda Petrusich") of _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ described it as centered on anxious love songs and similarly noted its movement between delicate [ballads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad") and more forceful moments.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-al-20) [Alexis Petridis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Petridis "Alexis Petridis") of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ highlighted the increasingly darker and episodic second half, in which songs frequently change mood, tempo, and arrangement before arriving somewhere different from where they began.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-ap-17)
Eilish sings throughout much of _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ in her signature restrained, [close-mic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close-mic "Close-mic") vocal style, frequently using layered [harmonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmonies "Harmonies") and [multitracked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multitrack_recording "Multitrack recording") vocals as an integral part of its production. _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork \(website\)")_ highlighted the record's dense vocal layering, while noting that its arrangements also include live drums from Andrew Marshall and strings from the [Attacca Quartet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attacca_Quartet "Attacca Quartet").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-hs-19) However, critics also highlighted moments in which she uses more powerful upper-register [belting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belting_\(music\) "Belting \(music\)") unheard on her previous material, particularly on "[The Greatest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Greatest_\(Billie_Eilish_song\) "The Greatest \(Billie Eilish song\)")" and "[Birds of a Feather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birds_of_a_Feather_\(Billie_Eilish_song\) "Birds of a Feather \(Billie Eilish song\)")".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-tc-22) In an Apple Music interview with Zane Lowe, Eilish said the album pushed her to expand herself vocally, more than any of her previous records.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-23)
### Songs
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Songs")]
_Hit Me Hard and Soft_ opens with the track "Skinny", which eases the listener into its moody soundscape with soft reverberated electric guitar, sweeping strings, and close, exposed vocals from Eilish. It is reflective and introspective, as Eilish analyzes her insecurities in a [stream of consciousness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stream_of_consciousness "Stream of consciousness") style, primarily addressing newfound adulthood, body image, and the pressure of fame and public judgment in the digital age.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-ap-17)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-24) The album then shifts into "[Lunch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunch_\(song\) "Lunch \(song\)")", a playful and sexually charged track with influences of [synth-rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-rock "Synth-rock")[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-25) and [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-26) The song uses playful food imagery as a metaphor for same-sex desire, emphasizing lust and physical attraction for another woman, and introducing a more explicit side of Eilish's songwriting.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-27) The third track, "[Chihiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihiro_\(song\) "Chihiro \(song\)")", features atmospheric, [house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music")-inspired production and pulsing [arpeggiated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arpeggio "Arpeggio") synths that slowly build tension over its five-minute runtime. Eilish's haunting, ethereal vocal delivery adds to the song's "hypnotic" and emotionally distant mood.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-theneedledrop-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-grammy-takeaways-29)
The fourth track, "Birds of a Feather", is a romantic and bittersweet [indie pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_pop "Indie pop") song with dreamy, new wave-influenced production and subtly morbid undertones.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-30) Lyrically, the song expresses deep devotion to a romantic partner through themes of unconditional love, death, and intense [emotional attachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotional_attachment "Emotional attachment"). Eilish has said this song pushed her vocally, as her brighter vocal delivery builds to what she called the highest belt of her career.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-31) "[Wildflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildflower_\(Billie_Eilish_song\) "Wildflower \(Billie Eilish song\)")" is a sentimental, slow-burning folk-inspired ballad centered on Eilish's experiences with guilt after dating a female friend's ex-boyfriend.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-33) The song begins with tender acoustic guitar and eerie ambient sounds before Eilish enters with an intimate, soulful vocal delivery.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-34) It builds to an emotional climax in the [bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_\(music\) "Bridge \(music\)"), where she sings "did I cross the line?" over crashing drums and guitars, then descends into a hazy acoustic outro with Eilish repeating the bridge's lyrics in a hushed tone.
"The Greatest", the sixth track, is a passionate folk and [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") song that critics likened to a mature successor to "[Happier Than Ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happier_Than_Ever_\(song\) "Happier Than Ever \(song\)")" (2021).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-36) Lyrically, the song finds Eilish attempting to process the devastating effects of a neglectful and emotionally absent partner, using the sarcastic refrain "man, am I the greatest" to express the emotional pain she endured in the relationship. The song [crescendos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamics_\(music\) "Dynamics \(music\)") into a heavier second half featuring electric guitars and belted vocals that heighten its cathartic intensity.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-al-20) "[L'Amour de Ma Vie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L'Amour_de_Ma_Vie "L'Amour de Ma Vie")" continues the album's shapeshifting sonic tendencies, beginning as a retro, jazz-inflected breakup song[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-al-20) with disaffected vocals and lyrics about moving on from a past relationship. Before it ends, the track flips into an energetic dance section, "Over Now", featuring emotive vocals filtered through [AutoTune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AutoTune "AutoTune") and electronic production drawing from [hyperpop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperpop "Hyperpop")[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-37) and 1980s [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-al-20)
Eilish narrates the role of a stalker on the eerie, minimalist "The Diner", which features creeping bass, off-kilter percussion, and dark, carnival-like electronic production. Critics linked the song's sinister, character-driven storytelling to the macabre sound of her debut studio album, _[When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When_We_All_Fall_Asleep,_Where_Do_We_Go%3F "When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?")_ (2019).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-grammy-takeaways-29)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-theneedledrop-28) The ninth and penultimate track, "Bittersuite", is a [musical suite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_suite "Musical suite") that blends immersive electronic and [downtempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtempo "Downtempo") elements as it moves through several distinct sections, while its lyrics explore private desire and emotional uncertainty.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-38) The track bridges into "[Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_\(Billie_Eilish_song\) "Blue \(Billie Eilish song\)")" through a hazy synth outro, foreshadowing the closing song's melody.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-39)
The closing track, "Blue", is a melancholic two-part song that reprises musical and lyrical [motifs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motif_\(music\) "Motif \(music\)") from earlier in the album while bringing its emotional themes to a close. Its first section, inspired by the unreleased track "True Blue", reflects on heartache, [emotional detachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emotional_detachment "Emotional detachment"), and the inability to move on from a failed relationship, using the color blue as a repeated image of sadness and regret. The second half shifts into a darker, more atmospheric passage about the emotional wounds of the person Eilish addresses, using imagery such as "born bluer than a butterfly, beautiful and so deprived of oxygen" to suggest [familial trauma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Childhood_trauma "Childhood trauma") and emotional deprivation.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-capital-blue-40) Eilish ultimately accepts that she cannot continue trying to change or save her partner, ending the relationship with empathy rather than anger.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-ap-17) It is noted for its use of lyrics from previous songs, bringing a sense of full closure to its thematic story. These include "I thought we were the same, birds of a feather", referencing "Birds of a Feather"; "désolée, mon amour" from "L'Amour de Ma Vie"; "I'm trying my best" from "The Greatest"; "don't know what's in store / open up the door" from "Chihiro"; "still overseas" from "Bittersuite"; and "a bird in a cage" from "Skinny".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-capital-blue-40)
## Release and promotion
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Release and promotion")]
_Hit Me Hard and Soft_ was released on May 17, 2024. It was available for [cassette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassette_tape "Cassette tape"), [CD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD "CD"), [digital download](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download "Music download"), [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_streaming_service "Music streaming service"), and [vinyl LP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinyl_LP "Vinyl LP").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-eo-41) On May 19 and May 22, Eilish released for digital download the isolated vocals, [slowed and reverb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slowed_and_reverb "Slowed and reverb"), and [sped-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sped-up "Sped-up") editions, respectively.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-iv-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-43)
### Marketing and tour
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Marketing and tour")]
See also: [Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft:_The_Tour "Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour")
In early April 2024, various news articles reported that billboards teasing snippets of lyrics for _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ had appeared in multiple cities in Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States;[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-44) although they did not mention the artist's name, her signature "blohsh" was recognized.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-45)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-47) The promotional billboards displayed [cryptic](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/cryptic "wikt:cryptic") lyrics, including "She's the headlights I'm the deer" and "Did I cross the line?"[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-48) Eilish later changed her profile picture to a "blue circle" and shared an image with the caption "Do you know how to bend?"[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-49) Eilish added her [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") followers to her "Close friends", a feature that allows limited accounts to see exclusive [stories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Story_\(social_media\) "Story \(social media\)"). The post features a "[lo-fi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo-fi_photography "Lo-fi photography")" image showcasing the artist's hand[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-50) and an image of her new [midriff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midriff "Midriff") tattoo.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-51)
Eilish previewed the songs "Lunch", "L'Amour de Ma Vie", and "Chihiro" during a surprise DJ set at [Coachella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella "Coachella") on April 13, 2024.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-52) In an interview published on April 24, she told _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ that she would not release singles prior to release. She explained that she does not like singles before album releases because she "really [doesn't] like when things are out of context" and compared _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ to "a family", adding that she "[doesn't] want one little kid in the middle of the room alone".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-rsalbumart-13) In May, a preview of "Chihiro" was featured in a _[Fortnite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite "Fortnite")_ trailer revealing Eilish's second in-game outfit. The song was also made available as a "Jam Track" to use in the _[Fortnite Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite_Festival "Fortnite Festival")_ mode alongside "Lunch" and "The Diner".[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-53)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-54) Furthermore, a snippet of "Birds of a Feather" was featured in a promotional clip for the third season of the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") series _[Heartstopper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartstopper_\(TV_series\) "Heartstopper \(TV series\)")_.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-55) Eilish held listening party events for fans at the [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in Brooklyn on May 15 and [Kia Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kia_Forum "Kia Forum") in Inglewood on May 16, in both cases premiering the album in its entirety.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-56)

On April 29, 2024, Eilish announced [Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft:_The_Tour "Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour"), her seventh concert tour, in support of the album. The first North American leg began on September 29, 2024, at the [Videotron Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Videotron_Centre "Videotron Centre") in [Quebec City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_City "Quebec City"), Canada. The 2025 leg, covering Europe and Oceania, started on February 18 at the [Brisbane Entertainment Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane_Entertainment_Centre "Brisbane Entertainment Centre") in [Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane "Brisbane"), Australia,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-57) and concluded on November 23 at [Chase Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Center "Chase Center") in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), United States.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-58)

"[Lunch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lunch_\(song\) "Lunch \(song\)")" was released as the lead single in tandem with the album's release, along with a music video directed by Eilish herself.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-59) The song debuted and peaked at number five on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-bbhot100-charthistory-60) It also saw international success, peaking within the top five in the UK,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-61) Germany,[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-62) Australia and New Zealand,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-63)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-64) and various European countries.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-65)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-67)

_Hit Me Hard and Soft_ received widespread critical acclaim.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-89) According to the review aggregator [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ received "universal acclaim" based on a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean") score of 89 out of 100 from 22 critic scores.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-MC-80) In a five-star review, Helen Brown of _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")_ praised how it "whispers its way through a marvelous maze of music to deliver some big emotional wallops."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-Brown-84) [Neil McCormick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_McCormick "Neil McCormick") from _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ agreed in his own five-star assessment, opining that the "heartbreak masterpiece" is "rich, strange, smart, sad and wise enough" to stand in comparison with [Joni Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joni_Mitchell "Joni Mitchell")'s _[Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_\(Joni_Mitchell_album\) "Blue \(Joni Mitchell album\)")_ (1971).[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-McCormick-83)
Writing for _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ , [Alexis Petridis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Petridis "Alexis Petridis") complimented _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ 's "beautiful" melodies and "distinctive" lyrical touches, but wondered if some of its elements could be "a little too opaque" for its own good.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-ap-17) _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ 's Thomas Smith felt that although Eilish wrote it for herself, she created a record that will "resonate harder" than anything she has done before.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-Smith-86)

## Commercial performance
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Commercial performance")]
### Streaming
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Streaming")]
On its release day, _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ received 72.7 million streams on Spotify globally, becoming Eilish's biggest streaming debut on the platform. It also debuted with over 500 million streams globally during its first week of release, marking her biggest streaming week ever.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-137) Upon release, it charted at number one on [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music")'s all-genre albums chart in 138 countries worldwide. Eilish was also named Artist of the Year for 2024.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-138) It was the second-most-played album globally on Spotify in 2024, behind [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift")'s _[The Tortured Poets Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tortured_Poets_Department "The Tortured Poets Department")_.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-139) On [Deezer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deezer "Deezer"), _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ was the most streamed album of the year worldwide.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-140) In 2025, it was the third-most-streamed album globally on Spotify.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-wrapped2025-141)
"Birds of a Feather" was Spotify's most-streamed song in 2024[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-142) and second-most-streamed song in 2025.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-wrapped2025-141) It also broke the record for the fastest song to surpass three billion streams at the time.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-143) On March 1, 2026, the album surpassed 10 billion streams on the platform, becoming the fastest album by a female artist to do so. It was Eilish's third record to achieve the feat, after _When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?_ and _[Don't Smile at Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Smile_at_Me "Don't Smile at Me")_ (2017).[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-144) On July 21, 2026, [BBC Radio 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_1 "BBC Radio 1") revealed that _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ was the 14th-most-streamed album of the 2020s in the UK, so far.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-145)
### United States
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: United States")]
_Hit Me Hard and Soft_ debuted at number two on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") with 339,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_units "Album-equivalent units") in its opening week, including 193.93 million on-demand streams and 191,000 album sales in its first week. Although it is her first studio album to not debut at number one, it marked Eilish's largest first-week units in the US, as well as highest pure sales.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-146) _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ also debuted atop the _Billboard_ [Vinyl Albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinyl_Albums "Vinyl Albums") chart, earning 90,000 units in its first week. It was Eilish's fifth consecutive number one, following _[Happier Than Ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happier_Than_Ever "Happier Than Ever")_ (2021), _[Live at Third Man Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_at_Third_Man_Records_\(Billie_Eilish_album\) "Live at Third Man Records \(Billie Eilish album\)")_ (2020), _When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?_ , and _Don't Smile at Me_ (both 2019).[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-147) She became the solo woman with the second-most number ones, surpassing [Lana Del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lana_Del_Rey "Lana Del Rey"). With this, Eilish has also spent 27 weeks atop the chart, the second-most overall behind Taylor Swift (52 weeks).[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-Zellner-148) All ten tracks debuted in the top 40 of the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-Zellner-148) On March 14, 2025, _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ was certified double [Platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification#Platinum "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) for moving two million album-equivalent units in the US.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-RIAA-149)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-150)
_Hit Me Hard and Soft_ finished as the fifth-best-selling album of 2024 in the US with 2,259,000 equivalent album units—of which 570,000 were pure sales—and also the second-biggest-selling vinyl album of the year with 340,000 copies. Eilish was the year's second-biggest-selling vinyl act, selling 520,000 copies.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-151) In 2025, it was the fifth-biggest-selling vinyl of the year, with 192,000 copies.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-152) According to _[Hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hits_\(magazine\) "Hits \(magazine\)")_ , it has moved over 4.2 million in activity since its release.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-153)
### Europe
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Europe")]
In the United Kingdom, _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ debuted at number one on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") with 67,100 album-equivalent units. It marked her biggest opening week in the region, surpassing _When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?_ (48,400 units), and also the second-biggest opening week for an album in 2024.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-154) It was certified double Platinum by the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") (BPI).[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-BPI-155)
In Germany, it debuted atop the [German Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Albums_Chart "German Albums Chart"), becoming Eilish's second number one album in the country since _Happier Than Ever_ topped the chart in 2021, and was certified Platinum by the [BVMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BVMI "BVMI").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-BVMI-156)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-157) In France, _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ entered at the number one spot on the [SNEP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SNEP "SNEP") albums chart with 27,710 units, becoming her second French number-one album. It has since been certified triple Platinum.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-SNEP-158)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-159) It became the biggest selling international album and fourth overall in the country, selling 172,965 units in 2024.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-160) It was also the biggest selling vinyl of the year, with 42,085 copies sold.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-161)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-162) In 2025, _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ sold 151,107 units in France and was once again the biggest selling vinyl of the year, ahead of Taylor Swift's _[The Life of a Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Life_of_a_Showgirl "The Life of a Showgirl")_.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-163)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-164) In Spain, it debuted atop the albums chart published by [Productores de Música de España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Productores_de_M%C3%BAsica_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Productores de Música de España"), making it Eilish's second number-one album in the country, and was certified Platinum.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-PROMUSICAE-165)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-166)
### Other markets
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Other markets")]
In Australia, _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ debuted at the top spot on the [ARIA Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Albums_Chart "ARIA Albums Chart"), marking Eilish's third album in a row to accomplish this feat in the country.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-167) Three of its songs reached the top ten on the [ARIA Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts"); "Lunch", "Chihiro", and "Birds of a Feather" charted at numbers five, seven, and nine, respectively.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-168) _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ topped the ARIA Albums Chart for five non-consecutive weeks in 2024.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-169) In March 2025, following the sold out Australian shows of the [Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft:_The_Tour "Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour"), it returned to number one on the ARIA Albums Chart for a sixth non-consecutive week, marking the first time since mid-July 2024.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-170)
On the [New Zealand Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Albums_Chart "New Zealand Albums Chart"), _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ arrived at number one,[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-NZ-171) and four of its songs reached the top ten of the [New Zealand Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Singles_Chart "New Zealand Singles Chart"); "Lunch", "Chihiro", "Birds of a Feather", and "Skinny" charted at numbers three, six, nine, and ten, respectively.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-172) _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ spent ten non-consecutive weeks atop the chart and was certified triple Platinum by the [RMNZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RMNZ "RMNZ").[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-RMNZ-173)
In Brazil, all ten tracks from _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ debuted on the _Billboard_ [Brasil Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil_Hot_100 "Brasil Hot 100").[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-174) Additionally, Eilish became the first international artist to top the [Artistas 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artistas_25 "Artistas 25").[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-175) It was certified Diamond by [Pro-Música Brasil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-M%C3%BAsica_Brasil "Pro-Música Brasil").[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-176)
According to the [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") (IFPI), _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ was the second-most-consumed album of 2024 worldwide; it also ranked second in vinyl sales, with 612,000 sold, and fifth in streams.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-IFPI_2024-177) In 2025, _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ was the eighth-most-consumed album of the year according to the IFPI. It also ranked fifth in vinyl sales, with 428,000 sold, and sixth in streams.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-IFPI_2025-178)
## Impact and legacy
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Impact and legacy")]
In 2026, [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") listed _Hit Me Hard and Soft_ as one of the 30 classic pop albums of the streaming era as part of their Spotify Classics, a program that highlights albums and songs whose influence extends beyond charts, trends, and momentary success. The audio streaming service added: "In a streaming era built on shuffling and cherry-picking, Eilish pushed against the norm, hosting arena-sized listening parties so fans could experience the record as intended. The album broke pop release rules by dropping without a lead single, letting audiences discover their own favorites organically."[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit_Me_Hard_and_Soft#cite_note-179)
